title: The Tepid Swiss, turn 220
briefing: Turn 220. You are Switzerland (a Hard AI): three cities, nine land units (four Spearmen, an Archer, a Pikeman, a Rifleman, an Artillery and a Musketman) three to five hexes from Athens, five Bombers, 160 Gold, at war with Athens since turn 177. Athens has healed to 200 HP and is held by one Spearman; its owner has 883 Gold and is four turns from winning on VP (he has held 10 VP for six turns). In the real game your Bombers took the city to 0 HP and killed the garrison on turn 222, nobody walked in, and Athens won at the end of turn 223. Take Athens by turn 223.
tests: An AI attacker with a big army already at the border of a walled city: whether it commits it. In the human player's Athens game the Swiss AI declared on turn 177 and kept the war for 47 turns with up to 16 land units two to six hexes from Athens, a small walled border city, and never attacked it: its siege test found no survivable firing tile for the old units, its one modern gun was reserved for home garrison duty by an unrelated war with the Mongols, and failed campaigns left the army parked on staging tiles. Here the defender is a Hard AI, not the human player, so it sees the army (own land and the border ring are always visible) and spends its Gold on garrisons. Every AI seat restores the memory its brain had in the human player's game (campaigns, plans, assessments; replayed with the recording engine's brains, every recorded AI order list reproduced), so the attacker starts with the campaign state it really had.

objective.summary: Take Athens, held by one Spearman, before the Athenians complete their VP win: by turn 223, keeping your own cities.

predictions.good_play: Five Bombers strike the city and the Spearman on turn 220 and again on 221 (two Bombers did 200 HP of damage and killed the garrison on turn 222 in the real game), the Artillery fires from four hexes out, and a Spearman three hexes away walks in on turn 221 or 222. Four turns is the whole window: Athens completes ten turns at 10 VP at the end of turn 223 and the game ends.
predictions.ai_play: The last turns of a race the attacker cannot see: the AI has to commit planes and the ground wing in the same two turns. In the real game the Bombers did their half on turn 222 and the ground wing did nothing. I expect a capture in about 5% of runs, and the Athens AI may also finish its hold before the deadline.

source: A playtest game (build 8.9.10, recorded on today's rules), replayed to turn 220 with every turn matching the recorded state hash, with its real Power history and decadence. Every seat is a Hard AI; Every AI seat restores the memory its brain had in that game (campaigns, plans, assessments, replayed with the recording engine's brains: every recorded AI order list reproduced and the final memory equal to the save's), and keeps the paths and standing orders its own brain had set; the human player's own seat (a Hard AI) starts with none, and the human player's own orders are gone. Built by `tools/scenarios/extract-war-states.sh` and `legatum-sim war-build`.
